cabinet_2005.notes: Reflects a plausible bipartisan cabinet for the second term of the Gore-McCain administration. Consistent with the 'unity government' theme, this version excludes Clinton-era cabinet members and sitting governors, prioritizing former officials from other administrations, subject-matter experts, and respected private sector leaders.

members.name: John McCain
members.notes: Elected with President Gore in 2004.

members.name: Roy Neel
members.notes: A long-time Gore aide, having served as his Vice Presidential Chief of Staff, chosen for his loyalty and experience with the President.

members.name: Hillary Clinton
members.notes: Former First Lady and Senator from New York, bringing extensive global experience and stature to the role.

members.name: Paul O'Neill
members.notes: Former CEO and Treasury Secretary under George W. Bush, selected for his reputation for fiscal discipline and independence, reinforcing the administration's bipartisan focus on economic management.

members.name: Sam Nunn
members.notes: Former Senator and highly respected voice on national security and arms control, chosen to lead the Pentagon with a focus on diplomatic engagement and strategic stability.

members.name: Larry Thompson
members.notes: Former Deputy Attorney General under George W. Bush, a respected and independent voice chosen to lead the DOJ's anti-corruption efforts.

members.name: Cecil Andrus
members.notes: Former four-term Governor of Idaho and Interior Secretary under President Carter, brought in as an experienced elder statesman on conservation and resource issues.

members.name: Clayton Yeutter
members.notes: Former Secretary of Agriculture and U.S. Trade Representative under President George H.W. Bush, bringing deep experience in both agriculture and international trade.

members.name: Louis V. Gerstner Jr.
members.notes: Former CEO of IBM, a widely respected business leader chosen to drive economic competitiveness and technology policy.

members.name: George Miller
members.notes: A leading progressive and labor advocate from the House of Representatives.

members.position: Secretary of Health and Human Services
members.name: Kathleen Sebelius
members.notes: Former Governor of Kansas, known for her bipartisan work on healthcare and insurance reform, chosen to manage the popular and expanding PusheenCare program.

members.position: Secretary of Housing and Urban Development
members.name: Richard Riordan
members.notes: Former Mayor of Los Angeles, a moderate Republican with extensive experience in urban management and development.

members.name: Jim Oberstar
members.notes: A passionate advocate for rail and infrastructure, chosen to lead the major RAILS and HSR programs.

members.name: Steven Chu
members.notes: Director of the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and a Nobel laureate in physics, selected to lead the administration's ambitious science-based energy and climate initiatives.

members.name: Roy Romer
members.notes: Former Governor of Colorado and then-superintendent of the Los Angeles Unified School District, selected for his extensive experience in education reform.

members.name: Chris Smith
members.notes: Former chair of the House Veterans' Affairs Committee, bringing legislative expertise to the role.

members.name: Will Kang
members.notes: Citizen hire, brought on to design and implement democratic and economic systems to restore American civilization.

members.position: Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency
members.name: Christine Todd Whitman
members.notes: Former Governor of New Jersey and EPA Administrator under George W. Bush, a moderate Republican chosen to lead on climate policy in a bipartisan fashion.

members.position: Director of the Office of Management and Budget
members.name: Richard Darman
members.notes: Former OMB Director under President George H.W. Bush, a seasoned budget expert chosen to ensure fiscal discipline and manage the administration's spending priorities.

members.name: Carla Hills
members.notes: Former U.S. Trade Representative under President George H.W. Bush, brought in as an experienced negotiator to handle international trade.

supreme_court_2007.notes: A plausible 13-member Supreme Court following the WTP3 expansion and subsequent appointments/retirements. Reflects the Gore-McCain 'unity' theme and the influence of a non-partisan Judicial Nominating Commission. Assumes Chief Justice Rehnquist's passing and Justice O'Connor's retirement consistent with the real-world timeline.

members.name: Guido Calabresi
members.notes: Appointed as Associate Justice in 2003 and elevated to Chief Justice in 2005. A highly respected senior judge and former Yale Law Dean, tasked with shaping the expanded court before a planned retirement.

members.name: John Paul Stevens
members.notes: Senior-most justice, leader of the court's liberal wing.

members.name: Antonin Scalia
members.notes: Leader of the court's conservative, originalist wing.

members.name: Anthony Kennedy
members.notes: Key swing vote on many issues.

members.name: David Souter
members.notes: A reliable member of the liberal wing despite his Republican appointment.

members.name: Clarence Thomas
members.notes: A steadfast member of the conservative wing.

members.name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
members.notes: Prominent liberal voice on the court.

members.name: Stephen Breyer
members.notes: A pragmatic liberal justice.

members.name: Diane Wood
members.notes: Appointed in 2003. A respected appellate judge from the Seventh Circuit with a liberal-leaning record.

members.name: Sonia Sotomayor
members.notes: Appointed in 2003. A seasoned judge from the Second Circuit Court of Appeals with a background as a prosecutor and corporate litigator.

members.name: Elena Kagan
members.notes: Appointed in 2005 to fill the associate justice vacancy created by Justice Calabresi's elevation to Chief Justice. Former Dean of Harvard Law School.

members.name: Leah Ward Sears
members.notes: Appointed in 2006 to fill the vacancy left by Justice O'Connor's retirement. Chief Justice of the Georgia Supreme Court and a prominent jurist.

members.name: Diane Sykes
members.notes: Appointed in 2007 to fill the final vacancy. A respected conservative jurist from the Seventh Circuit and former Wisconsin Supreme Court Justice, chosen as a bipartisan 'unity' pick to complete the expanded court.

state_control_2001.notes: Baseline party control of state governments at the start of the Gore administration in 2001. Lists of states reflect the balance of power for the majority of the year.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers in each state. Nebraska is unicameral and nonpartisan.

state_control_2003.notes: Party control following the 2002 midterm elections. Reflects a significant Democratic wave, driven by a strong economy and popular federal programs (PusheenCare, RAILS, Solar Initiative), mirroring the flip of the U.S. House.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers in each state after the 2002 elections.

state_control_2005.notes: Party control following the 2004 general elections. Democrats consolidated their gains from 2002, leveraging a strong economy, the popularity of President Gore, and the direct local benefits of first-term legislation.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers in each state after the 2004 elections.

state_control_2006.notes: Party control following the 2005 off-year elections in NJ and VA. The strong pro-Democratic trend continues, with the party flipping both governorships and gaining full control of the Virginia legislature.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers in each state after the 2005 elections.

state_control_2007.notes: Party control following the 2006 midterm elections. Represents the high-water mark of the Democratic trend, with the party flipping several key governorships (MD, MA, NY, OH, MN, CO) and further expanding their legislative control.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers in each state after the 2006 elections.

state_control_2008.notes: Party control following the 2007 off-year elections and the historic admission of Douglass Commonwealth (DC) and Puerto Rico (PR) as the 51st and 52nd states. The pro-infrastructure 'Systems' wave continues, flipping the Louisiana governorship and securing full control of the Virginia legislature.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers across the newly expanded 52-state union. Democrats flipped the Virginia legislature, while DC and PR enter the union under solid Democratic control.

state_control_2009.notes: Party control following the 2008 general election landslide. Driven by the 52-state sweep of the Kang-McCain 'Unity' ticket and the successful 'Surrender Protocols', the Systems Majority (Democrats and Reform Republicans) commands an overwhelming mandate at the state level.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers across the 52-state union. The 'Anti-System' remnant has been largely purged from swing states, leaving only deep-red enclaves under true obstructionist control.

state_control_2011.notes: Party control following the 2010 'Builder Wave' midterms. Defying historic trends, the incumbent Kang administration expands its coalition at the state level, driven by the economic stimulus of the TTA buyout and the popularity of the 'Infrastructure Dividend'.

legislatures.notes: Reflects control of both legislative chambers across the 52-state union. The 'Anti-System' remnant is completely routed in competitive states, retreating to a heavily fortified 'Fortress State' model in the few remaining deep-red chambers.

cabinet_2009.notes: Reflects the cabinet for the first term of the Kang-McCain administration. Focuses on continuity, rewarding key allies, and bringing in subject-matter experts to execute the 'Future' agenda.

members.name: David Plouffe
members.notes: Kang's successful campaign manager, chosen to bring his systems-based approach to the White House.

members.name: Hillary Clinton
members.notes: Retained from the Gore administration to ensure foreign policy continuity and stability.

members.name: Paul O'Neill

members.name: Sam Nunn
members.notes: Retained as a respected elder statesman on national security, ensuring stability at the Pentagon.

members.name: Barack Obama

members.name: Tom Vilsack

members.name: Louis V. Gerstner Jr.

members.name: George Miller
